analysis: The code creates a HashMap (samlData) and calls its put method multiple times. HashMap implements the Map interface and supports the put operation, so UnsupportedOperationException is avoided. HashMap allows null keys and values, so NullPointerException is avoided even if any key or value is null. ClassCastException is not applicable because HashMap does not restrict key or value types; all keys are Strings and values are Boolean, String, or null (which is allowed). IllegalArgumentException is not thrown by HashMap's put method. Therefore, all declared exceptions are avoided in this context.
answer: UnsupportedOperationException: avoided; ClassCastException: avoided; NullPointerException: avoided; IllegalArgumentException: avoided.
remark: No exceptions are thrown because the underlying implementation is HashMap, which fully supports the put operation, permits null keys/values, and does not enforce type restrictions that would cause ClassCastException or IllegalArgumentException.
